City of Austin.canvass_cite: Canvass by council is the City's practice (e.g. Resolution No. 20221121-001 canvassing Nov 8 2022, https://services.austintexas.gov/edims/document.cfm?id=397765). No Nov 2026 canvass meeting posted as of Oct 20 2026: https://www.austintexas.gov/council/2026/2026_master_index
City of Austin.counties_cite: https://votetravis.gov/wp-content/uploads/City-of-Austin-Orders.pdf p1 (Ord. 20260806-002 recital: City 'located in Hays, Travis, and Williamson Counties'); p7 Ord. 20260806-003 Parts 3-5 (central counting stations in Travis, Williamson, Hays); p14ff Ord. 20260806-004 Parts 11-13
City of Austin.majority_cite: https://votetravis.gov/wp-content/uploads/City-of-Austin-Orders.pdf p7, Ord. 20260806-003 Part 1: council members 'shall be elected by majority vote of voters residing in each respective district'; also Tex. Elec. Code §275.002 (cities >200,000 require majority), per SOS opinion HC-1 https://www.sos.texas.gov/elections/elo/hc1.html. Charter section itself not retrieved.
City of Austin.notes: Three ordinances adopted Aug 6 2026: 20260806-002 (bond election, Props A-B = 'Measure A/B' $260M parks, $35M libraries), -003 (council D1,3,5,8,9), -004 (charter amendments Props C-J). No mayor race. Prop I is the only citizen-initiated (Save Austin Now petition, certified sufficient June 22 2026) amendment. Council races are by single-member district: only voters residing in the district vote.

City of Elgin.canvass_cite: Prop A is a local-option alcohol election (Tex. Elec. Code §501.035). Under §501.109(b)(2) a municipal local-option election is conducted by the city and 'the commissioners court is considered to refer to the governing body of the municipality'; §501.151(a) the canvassing body declares the result. https://texas.public.law/statutes/tex._election_code_section_501.109 ; https://texas.public.law/statutes/tex._election_code_section_501.151. No canvass date found.
City of Elgin.counties_cite: https://votetravis.gov/wp-content/uploads/City-of-Elgin_Order-of-Special-Election-Ward-1-Alcohol.pdf p1-2 (early voting/ABBM arrangements for Bastrop County voters and Travis County voters); https://votetravis.gov/wp-content/uploads/City-of-Elgin_Notice-of-Special-Election_UPDATED.pdf p2 (Travis precincts within City for the local-option election: 490, 145, 146)
City of Elgin.notes: Elgin's order (issued July 21 2026) also orders a City Council Member Ward 1 election to fill a vacancy; that race is NOT on the Travis ballot (Travis notice covers only Prop A), so Ward 1 appears to be wholly outside Travis (presumably Bastrop) - not in our contest list. Bastrop County Elections Administrator: Kristin Miles.

City of Jonestown.canvass_cite: https://votetravis.gov/wp-content/uploads/City-of-Jonestown_Order-of-Election.pdf p3, Res. 2026-R-577 §13: 'the election returns shall be canvassed by the City Council not earlier than November 6, 2026, nor later than November 17, 2026'

County-only status inferred from the order naming only Travis.
City of Jonestown.majority_cite: Plurality: Tex. Elec. Code §2.001 ('to be elected to a public office, a candidate must receive more votes than any other candidate') https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/EL/htm/EL.2.htm; order §6 (https://votetravis.gov/wp-content/uploads/City-of-Jonestown_Order-of-Election.pdf p2) says the election follows 'the law governing the holding of general elections by general law cities'. No city majority requirement found (not exhaustively verified).
City of Jonestown.notes: Places 3, 4, 5 for 2-year terms (Res. 2026-R-577, passed Aug 13 2026). Order contains copy-paste references to 'November 4, 2025' in §5 and §8. Place 4 is uncontested.
